title: Receive transport creation can commit after viewer departure
test: tests/socketRecvTransportDeparture.test.js: 'create-recv-transport stores nothing, closes its transport and fails when the viewer left the room during the await', '... stores nothing and closes its transport when the viewer disconnected during the await', '... fails and stores nothing in either room when the viewer moved to another room during the await', '... fails and closes its transport when the room was destroyed during the await'
proof: On the unchanged code the leave-room, moved-room and destroyed-room tests got success: true instead of { success: false, error: 'Not in a room.' } for a transport allocated after the viewer was gone, and the disconnect test timed out waiting for the stale transport to be closed (it was stored in room.viewerTransports instead). After the fix create-recv-transport, once the allocation resolves and its state handlers are attached, requires socket.connected !== false, findRoomBySocket(socket.id) === room and findRoomByCode(room.code) === room; otherwise it marks the transport for shutdown, closes it, answers { success: false, error: 'Not in a room.' } and stores nothing. All four pass, the allocated transport is closed and absent from room.viewerTransports, and the ignored-transport count returns to its baseline (__testing.getIgnoredTransportCount). 'create-recv-transport stores the transport and succeeds for a viewer that stays' and the two overlapping-call tests (existing raced-transport cleanup) pass before and after.
